children: faces fresh scrutiny over AI spending, with shares at $511.41, down nearly 7.5%, at 11:55 a.m. ET Thursday. A higher analyst target offers a bullish counterpoint: Susquehanna's $620 objective sits roughly 21.2% above that price. The selloff shows investors still need convincing.

According to TheFly, Susquehanna raised its target from $550 and maintained a Positive rating, anticipating modest semiconductor earnings upside with AI leading the way. AMD has real profits behind that optimism. Second-quarter Data Center revenue reached $6.718 billion, generating $2.103 billion in segment operating incomea margin of roughly 31.3%. The next test is whether that earnings power keeps expanding.

Valuation leaves little room for disappointment. The GF Value graphic places shares roughly 74% above its $293.92 estimate, suggesting substantial growth expectations remain baked into the price despite Thursday's decline. AMD's third-quarter outlook calls for revenue of $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million, and a 56% adjusted gross margin. Investors need delivery on both sales and profitability to support that premium.

title: AMD Stocks Drop 7.53% as AI Spending Fears Challenge a $620 Target
